questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error from the given options.

In the evening he likes to read books and articles that have nothing to do of his work.
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 1.

'do of his work' is incorrect because 'of' is grammatically wrong. The correct word to be used instead of *'of' *is 'with' which means having or possessing.

__Correct sentence:__ *In the evening he likes to read books and articles that have nothing to do **with** his work.*

• Example: My father is in the room.
 
 
 
• "On" is used to indicate touching and being supported by the top surface of (something).
 
 
• Example: The keys are on the table.
 
 
 
• "At" is used to refer to time or place.
 
 
• Example: I will meet you at 9 0'clock.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 5.
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 4.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let us explore the given options:
 
 
• "As" is used to introduce two events happening at the same time. 
 
 
• Example: As the show increases in popularity, more and more tickets are sold daily.
 
 
 
• "While" is used when we have two continuous actions taking place at the same time.
 
 
• Example: He called while I was sleeping.
 
 
 
• "Whereas" is used as a conjunction used for showing a fact that is different.
 
 
• Example: you treat the matter lightly, **whereas** I myself was never more serious
 
 
 
• **"But" is used for introducing an idea that contrasts with or is different from what has just been said**.
 
 
• Example: She's very hard-working but not very imaginative.
 
 
 
 
 
• **In the given sentence, at first, it is stated that a powerful earthquake happens once every two years but after that a contrasting statement is given that when it happens it is devastating.**
 
• Thus, **the conjunction "but" will be used.**
 
• Hence, the **correct answer is option 4**.
